segments.content:
Chapter 107: 0104 Quietly Pulled Off Something Big

A slightly chubby girl stood up and asked, "Chen Guiliang, can you tell us about your entrepreneurial process?"

Chen Guiliang had an impression of this female classmate. He seemed to recall her surname was Liang, the Youth League Secretary of the Yuanpei Program, and the top scorer in the liberal arts Gaokao from some province.

As for her full name, however, Chen Guiliang had forgotten it.

"Yeah, tell us in detail. You're the only one in our class with experience," another boy chimed in.

"Tell us, come on, tell us!"

More and more people began to urge him.

Everyone was too unfamiliar with the students from other groups. Besides the class cadres, Chen Guiliang was the person most people knew. With not much else to talk about at today's gathering, a classmate starting a company was a much more engaging topic.

"Go ahead and tell them," Chen Guiliang's counselor, Long Xiang, finally spoke up.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Then I'll give a rough overview."

"I'm a kid from the countryside and haven't seen much money before. I got a reward of several tens of thousands of yuan for getting into Peking University, and I also earned a bit from writing. Since this money was just sitting around, I thought about whether I could start some kind of business with it."

"As it happens, I'm quite a fan of *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, so I thought about turning the characters into a card game. But I had no experience in starting a company, so I asked some senior students for advice, including my counselor, Senior Long."

"So I plucked up my courage and went to the Peking University Science Park to give it a try. It turned out my incubator project application was actually approved."

The Youth League Secretary, Liang Yuting, asked again, "What are the Peking University Science Park and the incubator project?"

The other students also pricked up their ears. Their focus had always been on professors, courses, and clubs; this was the first time they had ever heard of a science park at Peking University.

Chen Guiliang explained, "The Peking University Science Park was founded 12 years ago and is operated by Peking University Science Park Co., Ltd., which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Peking University. Until 2000, it was still in its initial phase, focusing mainly on infrastructure construction. For example, the Pacific Building next door was a joint development project involving the PKU Science Park company."

"Wow!"

A wave of amazement went through the crowd. They often saw the Pacific Building but never imagined the PKU Science Park had a stake in it.

Chen Guiliang continued, "Three years ago, the PKU Science Park was designated a 'National University Science Park.' Combined with the accumulation of the previous nine years, its funding became more abundant. So, two years ago, it established an incubator company specifically to support the entrepreneurial projects of Peking University students, faculty, alumni, and overseas returnees in Beijing."

"They've been focused on infrastructure construction these past two years, and many facilities are about to be completed. I was quite lucky, because with those buildings nearly finished, the Science Park shifted its focus to incubation projects. The level of support increased, more slots became available for entering the Science Park, so the review process was much easier than before."

"I first prepared a business plan. After the project was approved, the Science Park helped me handle the various licenses. Of course, I had to pay a certain processing fee for their services."

"I don't recommend everyone start a business right now. First, you should focus on your studies. Second, I'm not even confident myself; one wrong move and I could lose everything."

Another boy asked, "Your project is just selling this card game?"

Chen Guiliang recognized this person. It was Zeng Changgao, the academic representative of the science track class. The one with a super freakish memory, the reason Jiang Junlai chose 20 courses was to compete with him.

Chen Guiliang said, "The physical card game is just the first step. Next, I plan to launch a corresponding online game. It's currently in development, and we're hiring people for character voice acting next week."

"If the game's promotion goes well, I also plan to organize offline collegiate card game tournaments. I'll start by organizing the major universities in Beijing, then slowly expand nationwide. It would be even better if every university had a club related to Legends of the Three Kingdoms."

Hearing this, everyone was even more impressed.

These plans were far grander than just selling cards, which explained why it could become an incubator project at the Peking University Science Park.

Putting other things aside, just the idea of establishing Legends of the Three Kingdoms clubs in all major Beijing universities and organizing an offline intercollegiate tournament in Beijing was impressive. If this vision could be realized, Chen Guiliang would definitely become a celebrity, sought after by students at any university in Beijing.

The Yuanpei Program students found it hard to imagine how much money Chen Guiliang could make; what they could more directly feel was how famous Chen Guiliang would become in major universities.

Some even fantasized, if I were that famous, wouldn't finding a girlfriend be a piece of cake?

The 14 third-year counselors said nothing, instead communicating with looks and expressions. They were stunned by this series of plans!

Of course, the plan sounded wonderful, but whether it could be realized was another matter entirely.

Everything was predicated on Legends of the Three Kingdoms becoming a hit.

So, would Legends of the Three Kingdoms become popular?

"Chen Guiliang, why don't you teach everyone how to play? We can play and chat," said the female senior counselor from Group Seven.

The Yuanpei Program students were currently gathered in an open space by Unnamed Lake. Many were sitting directly on the ground, while the more particular ones only had a book under them.

The senior students gathered around, and Chen Guiliang immediately explained the basic rules.

After he finished, he had the counselors form a circle and then went back to his bicycle to grab a second set.

And so, 16 people started two separate games of Legends of the Three Kingdoms, while the rest watched from the side and chatted. More students couldn't squeeze in, so they broke off to mingle across different groups, talking about all sorts of things.

After just a few rounds, both those playing and those watching felt that Legends of the Three Kingdoms could definitely become a hit.

Because they were already hooked!

"Chen Guiliang, where can I buy these cards?" One boy couldn't wait to take a turn and wanted to go buy another set right away.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "The convenience stores nearby have them, 30 yuan a set."

The boy casually grabbed a bicycle, not knowing which Yuanpei student it belonged to, and pedaled off in a flash, disappearing from sight.

"Not bad, President Chen. Business is starting already," a girl joked, giving Chen Guiliang the nickname "President Chen."

Chen Guiliang said, "It's all thanks to my classmates' support."

Deng Chen from the dorm room across the hall praised, "You're the most awesome person in our class now. You've become a big boss in the blink of an eye. I heard from Yunfan that you've also become an inner disciple of Professor Yuan."

"Who's Professor Yuan?" a boy from the science track asked.

Yunfan explained, "The Dean of the Peking University Institute of Sinology."

"Holy crap!"

Several nearby boys swore, while the girls let out gasps of amazement.

Damn it, forget about the business, even the professors like him that much?

Chen Guiliang said, "That's a rumor. How could I be an inner disciple? It's just that I can go ask Professor Yuan for advice sometimes."

The female senior counselor from Group Nine asked, "So have you gone to ask for his advice yet?"

"I'll go next week." Chen Guiliang needed to organize his materials.

Going empty-handed would be meaningless and wouldn't leave a deep impression on Professor Yuan.

"You'd better hurry up then."

"Right, don't miss this great opportunity. As long as you have a good relationship with Professor Yuan, getting recommended for graduate school will be no problem!"

"I've attended Professor Yuan's class before. He loves Tao Yuanming's poetry the most. Aren't you good at writing poems? Write one in a style similar to Tao Yuanming's and take it to Professor Yuan for his critique. It doesn't have to be perfect, just something to make the old man happy."

The senior students all started giving Chen Guiliang suggestions.

Chen Guiliang was receptive to all advice, nodding at whoever spoke, though whether he would act on it was another matter.

For Chen Guiliang, today's Yuanpei Program gathering was a complete success.

The counselors and the entire class had now thoroughly remembered him, and with a very deep impression.

Returning to his dorm in the evening, he continued writing, trying to produce as much of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* as possible.

During the daytime on the weekend, Chen Guiliang went out again to promote Legends of the Three Kingdoms, this time heading directly south to the Renmin University campus—Senior Ao and two other students were handling the Tsinghua side.

In the blink of an eye, it was Monday. Chen Guiliang looked up the university-wide course schedule and learned that Professor Yuan was teaching another class.

After finishing his own class, he rushed out of the classroom, pedaled furiously on his bike, and happened to see Professor Yuan walking out of the Science Teaching Building.

"Professor Yuan!" Chen Guiliang shouted as he rushed over.

Professor Yuan had already forgotten him and just assumed it was a student greeting him, so he nodded and smiled in response.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm Chen Guiliang from the '04 Yuanpei Program. The last time you gave a lecture, you said I could come to your office if I had any questions."

Only then did Professor Yuan remember. "Oh, it's you. Let's walk together."

Chen Guiliang patted the back seat of his bicycle and joked, "How about I give you a ride?"

Professor Yuan was taken aback for a moment, then burst out laughing. "Alright, it's been a long time since I've ridden on a bicycle."

Chen Guiliang: "..."

The students who had just finished listening to Professor Yuan's lecture were mostly walking out of the Science Teaching Building at that moment. As if seeing a ghost, they watched Professor Yuan get onto a bicycle and be carried away by a student.

What was going on?

Weren't they afraid the old man would fall off?

Everywhere Chen Guiliang rode, he drew stares. It wasn't just students; even many teachers were stunned on the spot.

"It's just up ahead."

"Got it. Hold on tight, I'm pulling over."

Professor Yuan carefully got off the bike and watched as Chen Guiliang locked it up with five separate locks. He couldn't help but ask, "Is this to prevent it from being stolen?"

Chen Guiliang said with frustration, "Don't even mention it. The last time I listened to your lecture, I came out of the Science Teaching Building and my bike had vanished on the spot."

"Then it's my fault," Professor Yuan said with a smile.

The old man and the young man walked into the office.

As Professor Yuan was about to refill his teacup, Chen Guiliang took out a thesis. "Professor Yuan, please sit down and read the thesis. I'll take care of the water."

Professor Yuan did not refuse. He sat down in his chair, put on his glasses, and began to read the paper.

This thesis was about the annotation errors in *Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng*. It had been published in *Mengya* before, but not in a thesis format.

Now, Chen Guiliang had revised it into a proper thesis format and had also found more books in the Peking University library to serve as evidence.

The title of the thesis was now more tactful, using the word "discussion" instead of directly stating that the textbook was wrong.

Of course, there was no English section; Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to waste his energy on it.

Just after reading the abstract, Professor Yuan's expression turned serious, and he began to read on carefully.

He happened to be the lead chief editor for the next edition of the People's Education Press high school Chinese language textbook!

Moreover, he had already "taken office" in January of last year.

But Professor Yuan didn't have the time or energy for it; he was merely the editor in name. The executive editors were two other people, and the entire compilation team consisted of more than ten members from major universities across the country.

After refilling the teacup, Chen Guiliang stood quietly to the side.

Finally, Professor Yuan looked up and said, "Chen Guiliang, is it?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang replied.

Professor Yuan praised him, "It's very good to have a questioning spirit; you should maintain it in the future. I will forward this thesis to the compilation team for the new curriculum standard high school Chinese textbook. If all goes well, the new edition will be adopted next year."

"Then I'll take my leave now," Chen Guiliang said with a bow.

Professor Yuan said, "I'll give you my phone number. You don't have to come block me at the teaching building next time."

Chen Guiliang saved the phone number and quickly left.

Professor Yuan picked up his fountain pen and wrote his comment on Chen Guiliang's thesis: "Detailed materials and sufficient evidence. A valuable reference for the colleagues on the compilation team."

The matter ended there, and no one would speak of it to outsiders.
